brief:
Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in hopes of securing food for her family, Al-Monitor reported. A year after a ceasefire halted major fighting, hunger and malnutrition continue to stalk the territory as residents struggle to meet basic nutritional needs.

The prolonged food insecurity reflects the ongoing humanitarian crisis gripping Gaza, where access to adequate provisions remains severely constrained despite the end of active combat operations.
dek: Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family.
title: Gazans face severe hunger one year after ceasefire ends
